summary: One native run of loader-diag-xnu-rt-md1 (decision 0032). The 2.31 GiB donor-recipe APFS delivered into RAM was mounted by the donor apfs VFS as the kernel root (rd=md1), the donor stage0 and init ran (35 checks, 0 failed), Apple's own df, mount, ps -A and vm_stat ran, and exec /sbin/launchd.darwin was reached: ladder row 1a (pass) from the unchanged analyser. Reading the log by hand beyond the ladder: Apple's launchd (libxpc_executables-2462.120.4) ran its boot tasks fsck..fips, Apple corecrypto FIPS POST passed 18 self-tests from the dylib, libignition failed at stage preboot (errno 25, not fatal), and the keybag boot task died on the missing /private/var/keybags/systembag.kb and requested a reboot at kernel time 203.3 s. First Apple user space on this S24; no UI, display, input or GPU.

Boot tasks run in order: fsck, mount-phase-1, data-protection, finish-obliteration, detect-installed-roots, commit-boot-mode, restore-datapartition, mount-phase-2, init-with-data-volume, MSUEarlyBootTask, fips, keybag. fips: Apple corecrypto Module v13.0 FIPS POST, 18 tests PASSED in 238 ms.

The analyser's row 1a ('no PID 1 exit') does not capture this; the registered ladder did not anticipate launchd getting this far.
First USB return was Download Mode at dt 379.91 s (analyser class cap-reset, consistent with the 360 s deadline); whether the kernel's reboot path reset the SoC is not established.

native-device: Apple's launchd gets through ten boot tasks and the FIPS self-test; the first hard stop is the keybag task for lack of /private/var/keybags/systembag.kb.
not_established: That any launchd job or XPC service runs; the job list was empty by design.
That systembag.kb of some kind (or a launchd boot-task change) is enough to pass the keybag task; that libignition's preboot failure matters beyond its message.
That the kernel's reboot path resets the SoC; anything about display, input, GPU, backboardd or SpringBoard.
